data.title: Micron stock rises as RBC sees AI memory demand supporting valuation
data.description:
Micron Technology (MU) shares rose on Friday as RBC Capital Markets said the memory-chip maker's valuation does not fully reflect its exposure to the artificial intelligence-driven memory boom.

Micron stock gained as much as 3.12%. RBC analyst Srini Pajjuri reiterated an Outperform rating and a $1,500 price target.

Pajjuri pointed to rising memory requirements from AI workloads, including the shift towards more memory-intensive agentic AI applications.

AI demand keeps memory supply tight

RBC said memory demand continues to exceed available supply, with several structural constraints contributing to the imbalance.

These include rapid growth in high-bandwidth memory (HBM), limited clean-room capacity and tight availability of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) equipment.

HBM has become increasingly important for AI accelerators because it can provide high memory bandwidth for demanding AI workloads.

The expansion of agentic AI could further increase memory requirements as AI systems become capable of operating with greater autonomy and handling multiple tasks.

A Seeking Alpha report also argued that AI is changing the historical cyclicality of memory demand.

Memory consumption has traditionally been driven by equipment volumes and increasing memory content per device, making the industry sensitive to hardware replacement cycles.

However, Micron's margins have shown a prominent upward trend since 2022, while the company has also repeatedly exceeded market expectations in recent quarters.

Micron is scheduled to report its next results on September 30.

Valuation leaves room for expansion

Despite the tight supply-demand environment, RBC said Micron's valuation remains relatively modest.

According to Pajjuri, Micron trades at approximately 6.5 times expected forward earnings. He said this valuation gives limited credit to the company's Strategic Customer Agreements and floor pricing agreements.

RBC believes the combination of sustained AI demand, structural supply constraints, and customer agreements could support an expansion in Micron's valuation multiple.

Long-term contracts are becoming increasingly important in the memory industry.

Micron and its peers are securing agreements that establish future purchasing commitments for DRAM and NAND products.

These arrangements can provide greater visibility into future demand while reflecting the tight conditions across the memory market.

Capacity constraints support memory prices

The memory industry's supply response is constrained by the time required to expand physical capacity.

New facilities require construction, equipment installation, qualification, and increases in production throughput, which can extend the period before additional supply becomes available.

There is also high barriers to entry and a relatively small number of competitors with global scale and experience through previous industry downturns.

Capital allocation decisions have increasingly been driven by expected returns rather than attempts to gain market share through higher production volumes.

This dynamic has contributed to a gap between memory supply and demand and supported higher memory prices.

AI workloads could add another structural source of demand as larger models, wider context windows and more advanced reasoning capabilities require greater memory capacity.

For Micron, the combination of AI-driven consumption, tight industry capacity and longer-term customer agreements remains central to the outlook ahead of its September 30 earnings report.

data.title: BitMine stock is stuck in neutral: here’s why it is about to pump hard
data.description:
BitMine stock has held steady above a crucial support level as the company nears an inflection point in its Ethereum accumulation strategy. BMNR rose to $25.58, up by nearly 100% from its lowest level this year. This rally may continue after it formed a highly bullish chart pattern and as Ether steadies. 

BitMine stock rises as Ethereum rally continues

ETH token jumped and crossed the important resistance level of $2,500. It was trading at $2,595, up sharply from the year-to-date low of $1,517. This rally coincided with the broader crypto market gains, that pushed the market capitalization of all coins up by over 4% to $2.75 trillion. Bitcoin also jumped above the crucial resistance level of $80,000.

BitMine is one of the top beneficiaries of Ethereum’s surge because of its large holdings. It now holds 5.956 million coins, currently valued at over $15.4 billion. 

There are signs that ETH price will continue doing well this year. As the chart below shows, the token has formed a bullish flag pattern and is now slowly nearing its upper side. This pattern is made up of a vertical line and a horizontal channel.

In addition to a bullish flag pattern, the token has slowly formed a golden cross pattern, which is made up of a 200-day and 50-day moving average crossover. It usually leads to more gains by confirming that the short-term momentum is accelerating.

Therefore, there is a possibility that it will jump to $3,000, which is about 16% above the current level. 

ETH price chart | Source: TradingView

Transition from cash burn to cash flow

BitMine stock is rising as the company remains in a transition period. After spending 15 months in an Ethereum accumulation phase, the company is now moving towards cash generation and strategic initiatives. 

Unlike BitMine and other crypto treasury companies, Tom Lee has a strategy of owning just 5% of all ETH tokens in circulation. The estimated amount is 6 million tokens, meaning that he now needs to buy just 43,000. If the recent trend continues, chances are that the company completed the accumulation this week. Alternatively, it may complete the process next week.

After this, the company, which has about 3 employees, will transition from dilution into focusing on free cash flow (FCF). It will do that by staking its tokens through MAVAN, the validator network it built recently. With the staking yield being about 2.7%, it means that the company will generate about 162k ETH coins a year. 

The value of these coins will depend on the prevailing Ethereum price, and the company will be able to use these funds to repurchase shares, pay dividends, and make strategic investments. This explains why Cantor Fitzgerald recently boosted its target for the stock to $60.

BMNR stock price technical analysis

BitMines stock chart | Source: TradingView

Technicals suggest that the BMNR stock has more room to run in the coming weeks. It remains above the important support level of $23.67, its highest point in March, April, and May this year. 

The stock has formed a bullish flag pattern, a common bullish reversal sign in technical analysis. It is also about to form a golden cross pattern as the spread between the 50-day and 200-day moving averages narrows. These patterns suggest that the stock may rebound and possibly hit the key resistance level of $40 soon.

data.title: BMO recommends betting on a recovery in this semiconductor stock
data.description:
MACOM Technology (MTSI) stock is inching higher on Friday after a senior BMO Capital analyst – Harsh Kumar – issued a bullish note in favour of the semiconductor firm.

In his research note, Kumar upgraded MTSI to Outperform and reiterated his $335 price objective, which signals potential upside of about 23% from current levels.

BMO’s bullish call brings much-needed reprieve to MACOM shares that are currently down some 30% versus their year-to-date high.

Why is BMO Capital bullish on MACOM stock

BMO highlights that the recent pullback presents an attractive entry point, as MTSI stock’s forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple compressed sharply from the high-50s in June down to about 29x.

More importantly, “fundamentals have remained rather solid throughout, driven by data center and industrial/defense," he added.

A major catalyst lies within the hyper-scaler buildout: massive capex from cloud service providers and artificial intelligence (AI) labs powering next-gen compute and networking infrastructure.

This is, in fact, expected to result in a 70% increase in MACOM’s data center vertical in 2026, an impressive acceleration from the 47% growth recorded in the prior fiscal year.

On Friday, the semiconductor stock broke above its 20-day moving average (MA), indicating the upward momentum could sustain in the near-term.

What else could drive MTSI shares higher?

Beyond cloud datacenters, MACOM shares are attractive because the firm’s broad-based portfolio is finding significant momentum in specialized industrial and defense applications.

According to the BMO analyst, defense demand “remains resilient and space becomes a material contributor to growth next year.”

With its advanced high-performance analog and RF products, MTSI is expanding its market share across satellite communication, radar, and next-gen telecom hardware.

Investors should also note that the semiconductor stock has a history of closing both October and November in “green” – a seasonal pattern that further improves its near-term appeal.

How Wall Street recommends playing MACOM

BMO’s constructive call mirrors broader sentiment across Wall Street, where institutional backing remains overwhelmingly positive.

LSEG data reveals that out of 19 analysts actively tracking MTSI shares, 15 maintain either a Buy or Strong Buy recommendation, with the remaining four assigning a Hold rating. None recommend selling.

With the mean Street price target currently hovering around $395, the broader consensus agrees that MACOM’s continued decline of about 30% from its late-May record high of $418.90 offers an attractive entry point if you’re interested in holding it for the longer term.

Supported by the strong fiscal fourth quarter (Q4) earnings outlook and robust institutional ownership above 76%, the stock appears strongly positioned to turn its recent operational momentum into an extended market recovery through the remainder of this year.

That said, MACOM Technology Solutions Holdings Inc does not currently pay a dividend, which makes it rather unattractive for income-focused investors in 2026.

data.title: When will Bitcoin hit $100,000 again?
data.description:
Bitcoin could reclaim the “six-figure mark” by next year, according to a bullish forecast delivered Friday by Matthew Sigel, Head of Digital Assets Research at investment titan VanEck.

Speaking this morning with CNBC, Sigel said mounting fiscal anxiety and structural market shifts are laying the foundation for a meaningful rally.

With BTC currently hovering at $80,000 following a turbulent macroeconomic week, institutional appetite remains remarkably resilient, he added.

And as central bank liquidity shifts and sovereign debt swells, the crypto asset could rapidly mature into a macro hedge for institutional allocators globally.

What could drive Bitcoin back to $100,000?

Sigel emphasized that a major shift in market mechanics is distinguishing this cycle from previous runs.

Bitcoin's annualized price volatility has tanked by about 50% versus four years ago – signaling an asset class maturing under institutional stewardship rather than purely speculative retail trading.

Underlying this stability is a worsening global sovereign debt landscape.

Governments remain "over-indebted," forcing fiscal authorities into precarious positions that often favour hard-cap assets.

Sigel noted that traders are "really paying up" for puts over calls, yet simultaneous US Treasury bond buybacks have triggered aggressive short-covering rallies.

With policymakers unlikely to curb deficit spending anytime soon, any eventual easing of global monetary liquidity acts as an immediate "turbocharge for Bitcoin."

Institutional capital may push BTC price higher

Despite the broader macroeconomic crosswinds, underlying demand from key institutional capital pools remains rather steadfast.

Conversations across the wealth management spectrum – from independent financial advisors to trillion-dollar sovereign wealth funds – reveal a major trend: institutions are accumulating Bitcoin on pullbacks.

Moreover, VanEck anticipates explosive adoption in stablecoins, driven by policy friction between Capitol Hill and traditional finance institutions.

Sigel labeled it a “remarkable irony” that legacy banking lobbies are attempting to “re-trade” and renegotiate rules that were formally enacted under last year’s landmark GENIUS Act.

This regulatory pushback from traditional banks is driving market participants toward decentralized rail alternatives at a record pace, he added.

Legislative gridlock and the horizon

The path toward $100,000 is not without regulatory hurdles, as highlighted by Capitol Hill’s latest legislative stalemate.

The US Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act earlier this week, leaving broader market-structure definitions between the SEC and CFTC temporarily in limbo.

Nevertheless, crypto adoption continues to outpace legislative delay.

The broader market backdrop, marked by recent interest rate adjustments from global central banks and persistent sovereign credit risks, continues to channel institutional flows into digital store-of-value assets.

If fiscal deficits keep expanding while global monetary policy pivots toward easing, the calendar firmly favours Bitcoin bulls aiming for $100,000 in the coming year.

This would represent about a 25% rally from the price at which the crypto king is trading at the time of writing.

data.title: DraftKings stock is losing to prediction markets despite CEO reassurances
data.description:
DraftKings (DKNG) stock is slipping further on Friday amidst mounting pressure from specialized event-contract platforms, most notably Kalshi.

Kalshi is seeing a massive surge in sports wagering volume with the kickoff of the NFL season – eating into the near-term appeal of DKNG shares.

The rising popularity of prediction markets has weighed on DraftKings this year, which is currently down nearly 40% versus the start of 2026.

Prediction Markets proving a threat for DraftKings stock

Today’s sell-off challenges recent statements made by DraftKings’ chief executive Jason Robins.

In a CNBC interview aired earlier this month, Robins brushed off competitive concerns, saying it is a “complete myth” that prediction markets are pulling volume away from traditional sportsbooks.

However, fresh industry data from NFL Week 1 suggests a vastly different reality on the ground.

CFTC-regulated prediction platform Kalshi generated a staggering $14.6 billion in total volume, capturing roughly 76% of sports and parlay event-contract volume.

DraftKings’ own event-exchange initiative trails significantly behind, fueling widespread investor concerns that prediction markets are actually cannibalizing traditional sportsbook handle rather than expanding the total addressable market.

Note that DKNG stock currently sits decisively below its major moving averages (MAs), signaling bears are in control across multiple timeframes.

What else is hurting DKNG shares on Friday?

Adding to the competitive strain, underlying betting metrics reveal a notable cooling across single-wager handle entering the key fall sports calendar.

Overall CFTC-regulated sports-only handle declined 30% month over month in August to about $18.6 billion.

While higher-margin parlay and combination wagers provided a partial cushion by rising 22% to $18.8 billion, the significant sequential reduction in baseline single-ticket volume signals potential consumer fatigue and tighter discretionary budgets.

For a high-multiple growth pick like DraftKings stock, any broad-based pullback in baseline wager frequency threatens to impair sequential quarterly revenue targets and slow margin growth across core operating jurisdictions.

And DKNG does not currently pay a dividend either to incentivize ownership despite these risks.

Should you buy the dip in DraftKings Inc?

Reflecting these structural and macro challenges, analysts at UBS lowered their price objective on DraftKings shares today to $48.

While the investment firm maintained a Buy rating and still sees massive upside in DKNG, experts pointed to near-term revenue normalization, elevated customer acquisition costs (CAC), and sticky promotional spending required to defend its share against emerging prediction-market alternatives.

Investors should also note that DraftKings Inc.’s relative strength index (RSI) has crashed into the mid-30s, indicating intense selling pressure.  

All in all, caution is warranted in playing the Nasdaq-listed firm as higher state tax rates in major markets and decelerating growth in online casino gaming (iGaming) continue to limit its near term upside until volume trajectory begins to sow some signs of stabilization.

data.title: Accenture stock falls 4% today: here's why
data.description:
Accenture (ACN) stock fell 4% on Friday after Guggenheim downgraded the consulting and technology services company to Neutral from Buy and removed its previous price target.

The downgrade came as Guggenheim said its channel checks had not identified a corresponding improvement in demand despite Accenture shares rebounding 52% from their June lows.

The firm also pointed to job-posting data showing fewer openings and Accenture's recent push into the mid-market through the launch of Accenture Edge.

Guggenheim interpreted the move as an indication that demand from core enterprise customers remains challenged.

Despite the 52% gain from June, ACN stock is down 29% in 2026.

Analysts see limited improvement in demand

Guggenheim's downgrade adds to a mixed view among Wall Street analysts.

According to TipRanks data provided in the source, seven of 18 analysts have a Buy rating on Accenture, while 11 have a Hold rating.

Deutsche Bank also highlighted weak demand trends but took a different approach to its price target. The bank raised its target for Accenture to $175 from $136 while maintaining a Hold rating ahead of the company's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report.

Deutsche Bank attributed the higher target primarily to increased valuations among peer companies.

However, the bank's assessment of Accenture's underlying demand remained cautious.

The analyst said there was no discernible evidence of a rebound in spending and argued that AI-related investment remains concentrated in a limited number of use cases.

According to Deutsche Bank, that investment has yet to translate into higher budgets for traditional IT services.

Accenture's scale supports its business

Accenture remains a major player in technology consulting and professional services.

The company serves roughly 9,000 clients across more than 120 countries, providing strategy and technology services.

Its FY 2025 annual report highlighted a digital transformation partnership with UniCredit aimed at modernising technology across 13 European markets.

Accenture also reported that it has worked with 195 of its 200 largest clients for more than a decade, a relationship that supports long-term client retention.

For fiscal 2025, revenue reached nearly $69.7 billion, an increase of approximately 7.4% from the previous year. Net income was around $7.8 billion.

Revenue has also increased from approximately $64.1 billion in fiscal 2023, reflecting growth in the company's business over that period.

Balance sheet and competitive challenges

Accenture's financial position provides another part of the investment picture.

Based on its August 2025 balance sheet, the company had a debt-to-equity ratio of approximately 0.3x and a current ratio of nearly 1.4x.

The company also generated close to $10.9 billion in free cash flow, representing cash remaining after operating expenses and capital investments.

However, Accenture faces competition from large technology companies as well as newer businesses focused on artificial intelligence.

Its reliance on ecosystem partners for a significant portion of revenue also creates potential risks if those partners develop competing offerings.

Regulatory developments could add another challenge. Regulations such as the EU AI Act could require additional compliance spending and operational changes.

Geopolitical tensions may also make it more difficult for Accenture to forecast demand for consulting services.

With shares having recovered significantly since June while analysts continue to flag soft demand, the company's fiscal fourth-quarter results will provide investors with another indication of how enterprise technology spending is developing.

data.title: Volkswagen stock plunges as €10B hit forces 2026 profit outlook cut
data.description:
Volkswagen shares fell 5% after slashing its 2026 profit outlook on Friday, citing a sharp contraction in China's car market, the rising cost of its job-cutting plan, and a major write-down on its stake in Porsche AG.

Europe's largest automaker now expects an operating return on sales of no more than 1% for the year, down from its previous guidance of 4% to 5.5%.

Shares fell as much as 7.5%, marking the stock's biggest intraday drop in a year, and the selloff spread to rivals BMW and Mercedes-Benz.

Where the €10 billion hit is coming from

Volkswagen said it expects negative effects totaling roughly €10 billion to weigh on this year's results.

A €6 billion write-down on the value of its Porsche AG stake accounts for a large share of that figure.

The rest reflects provisions tied to a hard-won agreement with workers reached this month, which will double Volkswagen's planned job cuts to 100,000 globally.

China remains the core problem

China, Volkswagen's largest market, continues to be the company's biggest drag.

China's overall car market has shrunk by more than a fifth through August this year, hit by an extended real estate crisis weighing on consumer spending.

The decline has hit Volkswagen even harder than the broader market, as the company struggles to offer electric vehicles competitive with local Chinese brands.

Volkswagen's own first-half results, reported earlier this year, showed the strain building well before Friday's announcement.

First-half revenue stood at €158.1 billion, while operating profit fell 11.6% to €5.9 billion, an operating margin of 3.8%, already below the low end of the company's prior full-year guidance range.

China sales fell 20% in the first half of 2026, the company said in July, even as electric vehicle orders in Europe rose more than 50% in the second quarter.

A guidance cut that keeps getting worse

Friday's announcement marks the second time this year Volkswagen has lowered its 2026 outlook.

In July, the company cut its expected sales revenue range to between a 3% decline and flat growth, while still maintaining its operating margin guidance of 4% to 5.5% at the time.

That guidance has now been abandoned entirely.

Volkswagen has also been grappling with underused plant capacity in Germany, adding to its cost pressures even as it pushes through a broader transformation program covering products, technology and its overall business structure.

Investors will now be watching whether Volkswagen can stabilize its China business and offset rising costs through its restructuring plan, or whether Friday's 1% target becomes the starting point for further cuts rather than a floor.

Operating return on sales has fallen every year since 2022, from around 8% that year to roughly 6% in 2023, near 5% in 2024, and just over 2% in 2025.

The originally guided 2026 range of 4% to 5.5% would have marked a rare improvement on that trend.

Instead, the updated 1% forecast makes 2026 set to be Volkswagen's weakest year for profitability across the entire period shown.

data.title: Strategy, Coinbase surge as Bitcoin hits $80k again, SEC eases tokenized trading
data.description:
Crypto-related stocks rose sharply on Friday as Bitcoin reclaimed the $80,000 level and investors responded to a new US regulatory framework for tokenized stocks.

Strategy (formerly known as MicroStrategy) MSTR gained about 12%, while MARA Holdings rose 9%. Coinbase Global surged 10%, Galaxy Digital and Circle Internet Group each gained 7% and 6% respectively, while Robinhood Markets added 7.5%.

Bitcoin BTC climbed more than 5% to move above $80,000 for the first time in two weeks.

The cryptocurrency had spent recent weeks consolidating between roughly $75,000 and $78,000.

The gains came after the US Securities and Exchange Commission announced a five-year exemption that allows certain platforms to facilitate trading in blockchain-based or tokenized stocks and other securities.

SEC introduces five-year innovation exemption

The SEC's new "Innovation Exemption" provides tokenized securities venues with a five-year exemption from certain rules that apply to traditional stock exchanges, including the Nasdaq and New York Stock Exchange.

The exemption also covers certain liquidity providers, which will receive a five-year exemption from dealer registration requirements.

Tokenized stocks are digital representations of shares that can be traded on a blockchain.

The SEC said the framework is intended to address regulatory challenges that could otherwise make it difficult for platforms to comply with federal securities laws without potentially burdensome changes to their business models.

Platforms will have to notify companies before listing tokenized versions of their shares. They cannot offer the tokenized securities if the underlying issuer objects.

The SEC also said synthetic tokens that provide exposure to stocks through derivatives or other products will not be permitted under the exemption.

SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said the Innovation Exemption is intended to facilitate on-chain trading of certain tokenized stocks while maintaining investor protections and market integrity standards.

The exemption is set to expire five years after publication, while the SEC has invited public comments as it considers potential further changes.

Tokenized stocks could expand crypto platforms

The SEC said tokenized NMS stocks traded under the exemption must provide holders with the same rights and privileges as equivalent traditional shares, including dividend and voting rights.

Tokenized securities venues can trade eligible NMS stocks through permissioned automated market makers and liquidity pools, although the SEC has imposed limits on the number of symbols and trading volume.

Venues must also stop trading a tokenized stock at the same time as trading in the underlying stock is halted on its primary exchange.

They must provide public information about their operations, trading activity, and the activities of their affiliates.

The crypto industry has argued that tokenization could change how financial markets operate by allowing shares to trade around the clock and settle transactions more quickly.

The SEC also highlighted potential benefits including greater liquidity, lower transaction costs, self-custody and fractional ownership.

Coinbase has previously signalled plans to offer tokenized stocks in the US when regulations permit.

Robinhood, Kraken and other crypto exchanges already offer tokenized stocks in overseas markets.

Coinbase gains from regulatory clarity

The SEC announcement came days after the US Senate failed to advance the broader CLARITY Act, leaving the cryptocurrency industry without the comprehensive market-structure legislation it had been seeking.

Against that backdrop, Baird reiterated a Neutral rating on Coinbase with a $130 price target, while describing the SEC's regulatory development as positive for the exchange.

Baird said the exemption could allow Coinbase to offer tokenized equities with full shareholder rights, bringing its asset offering more in line with Robinhood Markets.

The firm also cited a rebound in trading volumes and favourable regulatory activity, as well as Coinbase's continued development of its "Everything Exchange" strategy.

The SEC's decision could also create a path for crypto-native platforms to compete more directly with traditional brokerage businesses.

Analysts said tokenized equities could eventually bring platforms such as Coinbase and Robinhood into greater competition with established firms including Morgan Stanley's E*Trade and Charles Schwab.

For crypto-related stocks, Friday's gains therefore came alongside a regulatory development that could broaden the range of financial products offered through blockchain-based platforms.

data.title: Saudi Aramco cuts off all crude to Europe next month after pipeline attack
data.description:
Saudi Aramco has informed at least two European oil refining customers that they will receive no crude deliveries next month, after an attack on the kingdom's key pipeline to the Red Sea, Bloomberg reported citing people familiar with the matter.

European customers normally receive Saudi crude through term contracts, guaranteeing steady monthly supply.

The report said those deliveries under long-term contracts will not happen in October.

The decision applies to all European buyers, the people cited in the report said.

The pipeline at the center of the crisis

Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, a 1,200-kilometer route carrying up to 7 million barrels a day from the kingdom's eastern oil fields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, has been shut since a September 10 drone attack damaged at least one pumping station.

Reuters reported on September 17, citing satellite imagery and industry sources, that three pumping stations were actually damaged, one more than initially assessed.

The pipeline had become Saudi Arabia's critical alternative export route after Iranian attacks brought tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz to a near standstill.

Repair estimates range from a partial restart within days to full recovery taking five to six weeks, the report said.

Europe scrambles for alternatives

European refineries typically receive Saudi crude via Egypt's Mediterranean port of Sidi Kerir, linked to the Red Sea by pipeline.

With that route now cut, refiners are racing to secure replacement barrels from the North Sea and elsewhere.

Poland's Orlen, which relies on Saudi Arabia for roughly 40% of the crude feedstock across its three refineries, has issued more than ten tenders since last Friday to secure alternative supplies.

At least three European refiners have already had September cargoes canceled or delayed as far out as November, according to market sources cited by Argus, with two more expected to receive similar notices.

European OECD countries imported 577,000 barrels a day of crude from Saudi Arabia in June, according to the International Energy Agency's monthly Oil Market Report.

Oil prices swing on the outage

Brent crude climbed as high as $108 a barrel this week before easing to around $104.84 by Friday morning, as Saudi Arabia moved to reroute some exports through the Strait of Hormuz to offset the pipeline outage.

WTI crude traded near $103.

Physical crude cargoes in Europe told a starker story, with some prices reported above $130 a barrel and North Sea Forties crude reaching $136.75, a sign of how tight the actual deliverable market has become even as futures prices moved more modestly.

Consultancy Rapidan Energy expects Saudi crude exports to fall by 400,000 barrels a day this month because of the outage, partly offset by higher flows through Hormuz.

"Risk remains skewed toward a larger disruption if the pipeline outage extends past September or Iran, the Houthis, or other proxy groups escalate attacks," the firm told clients in a note.

The disruption adds to a broader energy shock already unfolding this month, as elevated oil prices feed into inflation concerns that helped push the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates for the first time since 2023.

data.title: Apple stock: Analysts see upside as iPhone 18 Pro sales begin
data.description:
Apple AAPL stock opened 0.45% lower on Friday.

However, analysts remain constructive on the stock, pointing to potential strength in demand for the iPhone 18 Pro models and higher pricing.

Apple began selling the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max on September 18.

The latest models are priced $100 higher than their previous-generation counterparts, adding to expectations that the new product cycle could support revenue growth.

Evercore ISI raises Apple price target

Evercore ISI raised its price target for Apple to $380 from $365 while maintaining an Outperform rating on the stock.

The new target implies nearly 13% upside from Thursday’s closing price.

Evercore ISI analyst Amit Daryanani said the firm expects the latest launches to contribute to a stronger-than-expected iPhone refresh cycle.

He also sees potential for both unit growth and higher average selling prices.

Daryanani pointed to a combination of higher prices, a greater mix of higher-priced models and increased memory configurations as potential drivers of pricing.

Evercore ISI’s recent survey also indicated continued interest in the new Pro models.

According to the firm’s poll, 53% of respondents said they planned to purchase an iPhone 18 Pro or Pro Max, compared with an average of 51% in previous surveys.

The survey also found that 32% of respondents expected to purchase the Pro Max, up from 29% last year.

Daryanani highlighted camera and broader functionality upgrades on the Pro Max as factors supporting interest in the model.

Apple shares have gained 24% year to date.

LSEG data cited in the report shows that 27 of the 45 analysts covering Apple have a Buy or Strong Buy rating.

Bank of America sees support from carrier promotions

Bank of America is also constructive on Apple’s latest iPhone cycle, pointing to higher trade-in incentives from US wireless carriers.

BofA analyst Wamsi Mohan said the maximum trade-in credit for the iPhone 18 Pro Max has increased to $1,200 from $1,100 for the iPhone 17 Pro Max.

The increase is roughly equal to the $100 price increase on Apple’s latest Pro models.

Mohan reiterated a Buy rating and a $370 price target for Apple.

He said richer carrier promotions could help support demand despite the higher prices of the latest devices.

The higher trade-in credits could therefore offset part of the increase in upfront pricing for customers upgrading to Apple’s latest Pro models.

Morgan Stanley highlights Apple’s AI positioning

Morgan Stanley has also reiterated its Overweight rating on Apple, alongside Meta and Alphabet.

The firm said large technology platforms with scaled distribution and extensive proprietary data are well positioned to benefit from the development and adoption of personalised agentic AI offerings.

Morgan Stanley considers Apple, Meta and Alphabet among the companies best positioned in this area, citing the importance of distribution and unique data sets for agentic AI.

For Apple, the latest iPhone cycle therefore comes as analysts assess both traditional hardware demand and the company’s broader positioning in emerging AI-driven technology markets.

The post Apple stock: Analysts see upside as iPhone 18 Pro sales begin  appeared first on Invezz
